mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending increases.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over 3 months signals a strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over 3 months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows and corporate earnings are impacted.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of retail sales (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS/GDPC1 is above its historical median.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as wage pressures and consumer spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a high CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days in a regime of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and a decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% within a quarter signals a shift in consumer spending patterns, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth becomes decoupled from consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases & RSAFS decreases > 1% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.
